{{Probability fundamentals}}
'''Pairwise error probability''' is the [[Probability of error|error probability]] that for a [[Transmission (telecommunications)|transmitted]] [[Signaling (telecommunications)|signal]] (<math>X</math>) its corresponding but [[Distortion#Electronic signals|distorted version]] (<math>\widehat{X}</math>) will be received. This type of probability is called ″pair-wise error probability″ because the probability exists with a pair of signal vectors in a signal constellation.<ref name=Book1>{{cite book|last=Stüber|first=Gordon L.|title=Principles of mobile communication|date=8 September 2011 |publisher=Springer|location=New York|isbn=978-1461403647|pages=281|edition=3rd}}</ref> It's mainly used in communication systems.<ref name=Book1/>

==Expansion of the definition==
In general, the received signal is a distorted version of the transmitted signal. Thus, we introduce the symbol error probability, which is the probability <math>P(e)</math> that the [[demodulator]] will make a wrong estimation <math>(\widehat{X})</math> of the transmitted symbol <math>(X)</math> based on the received symbol, which is defined as follows:

:<math>P(e) \triangleq \frac{1}{M} \sum_{x} \mathbb{P} (X \neq \widehat{X}|X)</math>

where {{math|M}} is the size of signal constellation.

The pairwise error probability <math>P(X \to \widehat{X})</math> is defined as the [[probability]] that, when <math>X</math> is transmitted, <math>\widehat{X}</math> is received.

:<math>P(e|X)</math> can be expressed as the probability that at least one <math>\widehat{X} \neq X</math> is closer than <math>X</math> to <math>Y</math>.

Using the upper bound to the probability of a union of events, it can be written:

:<math>P(e|X)\le\sum_{\widehat{X}\neq X} P(X \to \widehat{X})</math>

Finally:

:<math>P(e) = \tfrac{1}{M} \sum_{X \in S} P(e|X) \leq \tfrac{1}{M} \sum_{X \in S}\sum_{\widehat{X}\neq X} P(X \to \widehat{X})</math>

==Closed form computation==
For the simple case of the [[additive white Gaussian noise]] (AWGN) channel:
:<math>
Y = X + Z, Z_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\tfrac{N_0}{2} I_n)
\,\!</math>

The PEP can be computed in closed form as follows:
:<math>\begin{align}
P(X \to \widehat{X}) & = \mathbb{P}(||Y-\widehat{X}||^2 <||Y-X||^2|X) \\
& = \mathbb{P}(||(X+Z)-\widehat{X}||^2 <||(X+Z)-X||^2) \\
& = \mathbb{P}(||(X - \widehat{X})+Z||^2 <||Z||^2) \\
& = \mathbb{P}(||X- \widehat{X}||^2 +||Z||^2 +2(Z,X-\widehat{X})<||Z||^2) \\
& = \mathbb{P}(2(Z,X-\widehat{X})<-||X- \widehat{X}||^2)\\
& = \mathbb{P}((Z,X-\widehat{X})<-||X- \widehat{X}||^2/2)
\end{align}</math>

<math>(Z,X-\widehat{X})</math> is a Gaussian [[random variable]] with [[Expected value|mean]] 0 and [[variance]] <math>N_0||X- \widehat{X}||^2/2</math>.

For a zero mean, variance <math>\sigma^2=1</math>  Gaussian random variable:
:<math>P(X > x) = Q(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \int_{x}^{+\infty} e^-\tfrac{t^2}{2}dt</math>
Hence,
:<math>\begin{align}
P(X \to \widehat{X}) & =Q \bigg(\tfrac{\tfrac{||X- \widehat{X}||^2}{2}}{\sqrt{\tfrac{N_0||X- \widehat{X}||^2}{2}}}\bigg)= Q \bigg(\tfrac{||X- \widehat{X}||^2}{2}.\sqrt{\tfrac{2}{N_0||X- \widehat{X}||^2}}\bigg) \\
& = Q \bigg(\tfrac{||X- \widehat{X}||}{\sqrt{2N_0}}\bigg)
\end{align}</math>
